newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens vs dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened on Thursday, posting marginal gains against the dollar due to unmatched but very modest dollar inflows, commercial bank dealers said.
Against the dollar, the Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 58.57, compared to 58.81, while against the pound the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 98.21 from 98.80.
Dealers said exporters hoping to cash in on rates were eager to sell their dollars -- "Not that it's a lot, but the fact that it's coming in is supporting the shilling," one dealer said.
Another dealer said the ball had started rolling towards a stronger shilling, albeit gradually, and importers had opted to stay out of the market, hoping to buy dollars later at a cheaper rate.
"The market is very thin. Demand is shallow," he added.
At midday (0900 GMT), dealers were selling the dollar at 58.40 compared to opening rates of 58.60.
The money market was liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at between five to 12 percent, compared to Wednesday's five to 15 percent.
